mutants.effect: Survival curves count patients who were still alive at last follow-up as deaths, so every curve drops too fast.

mutants.effect: Patients stay in the at-risk group after they leave the study, so later deaths look rarer and curves sit too high.

mutants.effect: The log-rank test overstates its variance when deaths are tied, so survival differences look less significant than they are.

mutants.effect: Fisher's exact test only counts tables in one direction, so mutual-exclusivity and enrichment p-values come out too small.
mutants.evidence: not ok 6 - Fisher's exact test: p in [0, 1], and the same for the table transposed or its rows swapped

mutants.effect: Multiple-testing correction skips a step, so a gene with a weaker p-value can be reported as more significant than a stronger one.

mutants.effect: Hazard ratios handle patients who die on the same day with a cruder formula than the one the method states (Breslow, not Efron).
